02_reddit-gym-membership-photo.json.title: The gym said there was no record I ever canceled
02_reddit-gym-membership-photo.json.script: They 'lost' my cancellation form? I canceled my gym membership in person, signed their form, and snapped a photo of it before I left, because a friend warned me this gym does this constantly. 2 months later they charged my card anyway and told me there was no record I'd ever canceled. I emailed the photo, timestamp and all, along with the manager's own signature on it. Support went quiet for a while, then refunded both charges, closed the account for real this time, and added a note apologizing for the 'system error.' Funny how the system only errors in one direction. So how many other members never thought to take that photo?

06_reddit-landlord-in-writing-only.json.title: He Said 'In Writing Only.' I Took Him Literally
06_reddit-landlord-in-writing-only.json.script: “In writing only?” My landlord ignored three phone calls about my leaking water heater, then demanded every maintenance request be “in writing, no exceptions.” Fine. I wrote him a letter. The next day came a second letter about mold starting to grow; then a third about the drywall now sagging. A fourth, a fifth, a sixth—one letter a day, every day. Each went certified mail, so he had to sign at the post office counter personally. Three weeks and eighteen signed letters later, he called me—on the phone, the thing he banned—screaming that the county opened a habitability case from his own paper trail. Eighteen dated, signed letters make a beautifully airtight timeline of neglect. He fixed the heater within 48 hours. So who really regretted “in writing, no exceptions”?

02_reddit-upstairs-neighbor-noise.json.title: He Wouldn't Stop The Music. So I Got Creative
02_reddit-upstairs-neighbor-noise.json.script: My upstairs neighbor played bass-heavy music at full volume past midnight for months, and management's only advice was 'just knock on his door.' So I did something else instead. I found out he worked nights and slept during the day, then I filed a noise complaint every single afternoon between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. for 'a barking dog,' 'a vacuum,' 'construction sounds' — anything vague enough that management had to send someone to check every time, which meant knocking on his door and waking him up, over and over, for weeks. He complained to management that people kept disturbing his sleep for no reason. Management told him, very politely, that they were simply responding to resident complaints and had no way to verify who filed them. Three weeks of interrupted sleep later, his music stopped at 9 p.m. sharp, every single night, like clockwork. Turns out nobody actually enjoys a taste of their own noise.

06_boss-wanted-every-email.json.title: My Boss Wanted Every Email. He Got Every Email.
06_boss-wanted-every-email.json.script: My boss wanted every email. He announced that nobody could send anything without copying him because he needed 'complete visibility'—his exact phrase. Fine. I updated every automated alert, calendar notice, shared-document comment, delivery receipt, and ticket notification to include him. Nothing fake—just the messages our systems already generated all day. By lunch, his inbox had hundreds. By Wednesday, he missed a client's urgent approval because it was buried between a printer alert and twelve calendar updates. Complete visibility had become complete camouflage. He called me in and asked why I had flooded him. I showed him his own written rule and the audit log proving every message was legitimate. He quietly changed the policy to 'copy me only on decisions requiring approval.' I followed that one too. His inbox recovered, the client's request got handled, and the new rule lasted. Apparently visibility works better when you can still see.

05_bag-check-overtime.json.title: My Manager's Bag Checks Became Paid Overtime
05_bag-check-overtime.json.script: Every bag, seriously? Our new manager decided employees were stealing and ordered mandatory bag checks before anyone could leave. The catch was that two supervisors had to witness each inspection, and night shift usually had one supervisor total. So we clocked out, waited by the locked office, and wrote down every minute. After payroll explained that required waiting time was still work time, we stayed clocked in instead. Ten people waiting twenty minutes each night became a very expensive little security theater. By Friday, overtime had swallowed more money than the manager claimed was missing all month. Corporate asked for his evidence. He had none—just a feeling and a laminated checklist. The following Monday, bag checks became random, one witness was enough, and nobody waited off the clock. Apparently suspicion gets much more efficient when payroll starts billing by the minute.

06_manager-package-warehouse.json.title: He Banned Desk Deliveries. His Office Became a Warehouse.
06_manager-package-warehouse.json.script: Personal packages are unprofessional! That was our office manager's announcement after one small box appeared at reception. His new rule said every personal delivery had to be addressed to the department head and stored in his office until pickup. Fine. Holiday shopping started the next week, and twenty-seven employees followed the policy exactly. His office collected dog food, paper towels, birthday balloons, a desk chair, and one heroic flat-packed bookcase. Nothing blocked an exit; it just turned his workspace into the world's least convenient warehouse. He complained that people were abusing the system. We showed HR his memo, including the sentence requiring his name and office number on every label. HR asked him whether he wanted the rule enforced or deleted. It vanished before lunch. Reception got a package shelf, employees got one delivery a week, and his office became an office again. Apparently boxes look less professional when they're all addressed to you.

05_reddit-hardware-store-mistaken-staff..title: The Customer Insisted I Worked There. Fine.
05_reddit-hardware-store-mistaken-staff..script: Fourth time that hour, a stranger grabbed my arm demanding to know where the drywall screws were. I don't work at this hardware store, I just wear a lot of orange. She cut off my "I don't work here" with "don't play games, I need help now." Fine. I walked her confidently to aisle twelve, pointed past the pool noodles, and told her drywall screws come in bulk boxes near the register, technically true since I'd seen a promo bin there that morning. She marched off triumphant. Ten minutes later an actual employee found her arguing with a cashier about being sent to buy pool floats for a bathroom renovation. Store security pulled the aisle camera and the whole break room had a good laugh at customer service's expense. I finished my paint run in total peace. Nobody has grabbed my arm at that store since. I stopped wearing orange there entirely.

06_reddit-driveway-parking-trash-cans.js.title: He Blocked My Driveway. I Just Stopped Moving My Trash Cans.
06_reddit-driveway-parking-trash-cans.js.script: He parked across our shared driveway every morning, blocking my car in for "just five minutes" that stretched to forty. I asked nicely three times. He shrugged and said the city never tickets there anyway. So I started paying attention to exactly when parking enforcement swept our block, turns out it's eight fourteen a.m. sharp, right when his car was always sitting there. I didn't call anyone. I didn't need to. I just stopped moving my trash cans out of the second spot at eight like I used to, so the officer had a clean sightline to his bumper instead of mine. Three tickets in eight days, then a boot on the fourth. He knocked on my door convinced I had reported him. I told him, truthfully, I hadn't dialed a single number. He moved his car onto his own driveway the very next morning, and it has been there every day since.

05_reddit-return-policy-maximum-effort.j.title: She Demanded I Follow the Return Policy. I Did.
05_reddit-return-policy-maximum-effort.j.script: She slid a blender across the counter with no receipt and said corporate policy required me to accept any return regardless of proof of purchase. I don't argue with retail rules, I follow them, so I pulled up the actual policy on the register screen and read it out loud: returns without a receipt require a valid government ID, store credit only, and a mandatory fifteen minute manager verification call. She said fine, and handed over her license. Fine. I called the verification line, which put us on hold for twenty-two minutes while she stood there tapping her foot. When the rep finally picked up, the blender's serial number came back registered to a different store four states away, purchased in 2019. Store credit only, expired promotions excluded, prorated for five years of use: total refund, four dollars and twelve cents. She said that wasn't what she meant by the policy. I told her it was exactly what she asked for. She left without the four dollars.

06_reddit-birthday-party-refund-demand.j.title: She Wanted a Refund for Kids Who Never Showed Up
06_reddit-birthday-party-refund-demand.j.script: I run a small bounce house party rental out of my garage, cash deposit required, no refunds within 48 hours, printed right on the contract she signed. The morning after the party she calls, furious, demanding money back because only six of the twelve kids she invited showed up to her son's party. Not my fault, not my policy, I told her the inflatable ran the full four hours regardless of headcount. She said she'd leave a one star review unless I refunded the difference per absent kid. Fine. I told her to send screenshots of the RSVPs proving exactly six kids were confirmed, per my terms for partial refunds on no-shows. She sent them. Every single RSVP said yes. All twelve. She'd double invited half the guest list and blamed me for her own group chat. I posted the screenshots in my reply to her review instead of refunding a cent. The review came down within the hour.

05_reddit-entitled-parent-starting-lineu.title: She Wanted Her Son Starting Every Game. I Read Her The Rule.
05_reddit-entitled-parent-starting-lineu.script: She cornered me at halftime, arms crossed, demanding her son start every single game because they paid the same registration fee as everyone else. I run the rec league schedule, so I pulled up the bylaw on my phone and read it out loud: guaranteed EQUAL PLAYING TIME, not equal starts. She said fine, make him a starter then. So the next game, I did exactly that. Her son started. Ninety seconds later, right on the rotation clock, I subbed him out like every other kid on the roster. He started the next five games too, for ninety seconds each, technically undefeated as a starter. She showed up furious, waving the same rule she'd quoted at me. I handed her the printed schedule with her own words highlighted in yellow. By the final game, the other parents were timing his starts on their phones and cheering when the whistle blew. Her son quietly asked to just play normal minutes like everybody else.

06_reddit-price-match-bluff-print-shop.j.title: He Demanded A Price Match. We Called To Confirm It.
06_reddit-price-match-bluff-print-shop.j.script: He slapped a crumpled flyer on my counter and said the print shop across town charged half what we did, so I'd better match it or he was calling corporate. I told him our policy requires a verified quote, so I'd happily call them right now, on speaker, with him standing right there. He said fine, sure, go ahead, clearly expecting me to back down first. I dialed. A very confused employee on the other end read us their current price for the same order, and it was actually higher than ours, because the flyer in his hand was two years old, printed before their last rate increase. He stood there listening to his own bluff fall apart in real time, mumbled something about a special promotion, and pushed his card across the counter without another word. I rang up the full price, stapled the outdated flyer to the receipt, and wrote PRICE MATCH: DENIED BY THE COMPETITOR right across the top in red marker.

05_reddit-unpaid-driveway-lien.json.title: He Sat On My Invoice For Two Months. I Sat On His Closing.
05_reddit-unpaid-driveway-lien.json.script: Who froze the closing? I paved a driveway for a general contractor on net-30. Then he went silent for two months while selling that exact property for eight hundred grand. Emails ignored. Calls ignored. He forgot that I still had the signed work order, and state law let unpaid subcontractors file a mechanic's lien against the property, something most GCs forget. So I filed it three days before closing. The title company found it in escrow and froze the whole sale. His buyer's lawyer started screaming, and an invoice ignored for two months got paid in full within four hours, plus statutory penalty interest. He called it a misunderstanding. I called it pending. The lien release left only after the wire cleared. It took nine minutes. Would you ignore the driveway invoice again?

05_reddit-sign-off-flood.json.title: He Made Every Favor Need His Sign-Off. So I Sent Every Favor.
05_reddit-sign-off-flood.json.script: Our new manager decided every customer favor now needed his written sign-off, even a free bag. Fine. I started emailing him for approval on everything. A customer wanted a free bag? I cc'd him. A regular asked where the bathroom was? I cc'd him too, just to be safe. Sixty emails a day, every single one technically required by his own new rule. By day three his inbox held four hundred unread messages, and corporate started asking why he wasn't answering real requests. He called me into the office, furious, and told me to just use common sense. I told him common sense was exactly what got banned on day one of his new rule. He didn't have an answer for that. The sign-off rule disappeared from the break room wall within a week, and the free bags quietly came back.

06_reddit-wifi-throttle.json.title: He Kept Stealing My WiFi. I Just Started Throttling It.
06_reddit-wifi-throttle.json.script: My neighbor had been stealing my WiFi for a year before I finally said something. He said sure, no problem, he'd stop, then I watched his laptop show up on my router that same night. So I stopped saying anything and just throttled his device to dial-up speeds instead, three hours every evening, right when he sat down to stream something. A week later he complained to me that his internet had gotten terrible lately and asked if mine was doing the same thing. I told him mine worked perfectly fine, which was true, because it was mine. This went on for two months before he finally broke down and bought his own plan. The week his new router showed up, my network usage dropped in half, and I finally understood exactly how much of my bandwidth he had been eating the whole time.

05_reddit-karen-cup-review.json.title: She Threatened A Bad Review Over Free Coffee. So I Let Her Have It.
05_reddit-karen-cup-review.json.script: A regular tried to pay with a gift card from a store we don't even carry, then got furious when it wouldn't scan. She demanded a free drink for the inconvenience and said she'd leave a one star review if I refused. Fine. I made her drink and wrote her order under her actual name on the cup, exactly as she gave it, nothing extra. That night she posted the review anyway, bragging with a photo of the cup, proof she'd gotten free coffee by threatening a teenager. Corporate saw it within the hour. They didn't just delete the review, they pulled her loyalty account number off every location in the chain and replied to the post explaining exactly why. She showed up the next morning demanding to know why her app wouldn't load. I pointed at the conduct policy taped to the register and let her read it herself.

06_reddit-mistaken-employee-raise.json.title: She Wouldn't Stop Ordering Me Around. So I Started Doing The Job.
06_reddit-mistaken-employee-raise.json.script: A woman at the hardware store kept mistaking me for staff, shoving paint cans into my hands and barking aisle numbers like I worked there. Third time it happened in ten minutes I gave up correcting her and just started answering, mostly to see how far it would go. I pointed her to the right bolts, mixed a paint color from memory, even walked her to the checkout. The actual manager watched the whole thing from the office window, and when the woman finally left happy, he came over and asked how long I'd been working there. I told him about four minutes. He laughed, then asked if I wanted to make it official, because I'd just outperformed two people on his actual payroll. I filled out the application in the break room I definitely wasn't supposed to be in, and started training the following Monday.

05_reddit-hoa-garden-gnome-bylaws.json.title: She Fined Me Over A Garden Gnome. So I Read Every Bylaw.
05_reddit-hoa-garden-gnome-bylaws.json.script: Our HOA president left a $150 fine on my door for unapproved yard decor, meaning one ceramic gnome my grandmother gave me. The bylaws never mention gnomes, so I actually read all forty pages that night. Turns out half the street was already in violation of something: unregistered trailers, a trampoline over the height limit, a shed built without a permit, and one parked boat sitting in her own driveway for three years. I filed one formal complaint per violation, cited the exact clause each time, and copied the whole board. The next meeting ran four hours. Neighbors who'd never spoken to each other suddenly had opinions about setback rules. By the time the dust settled, the board voted to grandfather in most of it, my fine got dropped for lack of a written decor policy, and the gnome stayed exactly where it was, now with a tiny sign that says approved.

06_reddit-wrong-store-coupon.json.title: She Waved A Rival Store's Coupon At Me. I Just Called The Number.
06_reddit-wrong-store-coupon.json.script: A woman shoved a coupon across the counter insisting our system was glitching because it wouldn't scan her forty percent off code. She got loud fast, said she'd been a loyal customer for ten years, and demanded I override it manually. Store policy says I can call the printed number on any coupon to verify it live, so I did, right there on speaker so she could hear too. The automated line that picked up was not ours. It was a rival chain two blocks over, reading back its own return policy in a cheerful robotic voice. She'd grabbed the wrong flyer off her kitchen counter that morning and never noticed the logo. I offered her our actual weekly discount instead, ten percent, no drama. She took it without a word, and the coupon stayed folded on the counter until the next customer used it as a napkin.

05_reddit-clock-in-exactly-on-time.json.title: He Banned Early Clock-Ins. So I Stopped Clocking In Early.
05_reddit-clock-in-exactly-on-time.json.script: My new manager posted a memo: no clocking in early, not even sixty seconds, because unpaid labor is unpaid labor, clearly aimed at the two of us who always started fifteen minutes early to prep the queue. Fine. I set an alarm and clocked in at exactly nine o'clock every single day, and refused to answer a message before that second. Turns out those fifteen minutes were the only reason his nine-fifteen report ever went out on time. The first week, it was late. The second week, it was late and wrong, because nobody had pre-sorted the queue. By the third week he was standing at my desk at eight fifty-nine, watching the clock like it owed him money. He pulled me into his office, said the policy was more of a guideline, and asked if I would consider coming back fifteen minutes early, paid this time, and backdated to the memo. I said I would think about it. I clocked in at exactly nine o'clock the next morning too.

06_reddit-gym-arbitration-clause.json.title: My Gym Wouldn't Let Me Cancel. So I Read The Contract.
06_reddit-gym-arbitration-clause.json.script: My gym's cancellation policy was one sentence in twelve-point font: cancel in person, in writing, thirty days out, notarized. I work night shift and the gym closes at nine, so I mailed a certified letter instead. They never received it three separate times and kept charging my card forty-nine ninety-nine a month for a gym I had not stepped into since March. So I pulled the contract and found their own arbitration clause, the one meant to stop customers from suing them, required THEM to pay a nineteen hundred dollar filing fee just to respond to any dispute. I filed one. The gym's corporate office called within four days, offered a full refund for every month since March, and asked, very politely, if I would be willing to withdraw the claim. I said I would think about it, cashed the refund check, and let the filing fee clock run out anyway.

05_reddit-email-everything.json.title: He Said Email Everything. So I Did.
05_reddit-email-everything.json.script: My new supervisor hated 'wasting time' on hallway questions, so he posted a memo: every request goes through email, no exceptions, effective immediately. Fine by me — I stopped answering anyone who just walked up to my desk, no matter how small the ask. Day one, seven emails piled into his inbox before lunch, every one a two-line question he used to wave off verbally in ten seconds. By day four he had ninety-one unread messages and a folder titled 'URGENT' with fourteen items in it, half of them from himself asking where things were. Day five he called an all-staff meeting to announce that verbal requests were, actually, fine again, small ones especially, and could everyone please stop CC'ing him on literally everything. I printed his original memo, framed it, and hung it directly above my monitor. He walked past it every single day and never once said a word about taking it down.

06_reddit-dont-work-here.json.title: She Wouldn't Believe I Don't Work Here. So I Helped.
06_reddit-dont-work-here.json.script: I was standing in the paint aisle for four minutes, in street clothes, holding my own basket, when a woman marched up demanding to know why nobody had restocked the drop cloths. I told her, twice, I didn't work there. She said 'don't play dumb' and pointed at a shelf, so I stopped arguing and became the single most confident employee that store never hired. I told her the drop cloths were discontinued, the good ones were two aisles over by the pet food, and the industrial size was 'in the back, by returns.' She thanked me and marched off toward dog treats. Ninety seconds later an actual employee in a red vest walked past, and she flagged him down demanding to know why his coworker sent her to the wrong aisle on purpose. He had no idea what she was talking about. I was already checking out.
